detail.longDescription:
I'm building a "move this block" feature for a TinyMCE 6 editor. The blocks are top-level
s in the editor body, and I move them with plain DOM calls inside editor.undoManager.transact() so that the move is one undo step. The move itself works, but undoManager.undo() doesn't take me back to the content as it was just before the move. It goes back further, to the state before the content was loaded with setContent() . 
   Click the three buttons in order (TinyMCE 6.8.6 from the CDN, Chrome): after setContent: A,B,C after move: C,A,B after undo(): (empty) What I expected after undo(): A,B,C , i.e. the document as it was right before the move. What I found If I call editor.undoManager.add() before transact() , undo behaves as expected: ed.setContent('
A
B
C
'); ed.undoManager.add(); // <-- added ed.undoManager.transact(() => { const body = ed.getBody(); body.insertBefore(body.lastElementChild, body.firstElementChild); }); ed.undoManager.undo(); // now gives A,B,C My understanding is that setContent() does not add an undo level for the new content, so when transact() finishes it records only the after state, and there is no level for the before state to return to. Questions Is that the right explanation, i.e. is it expected that setContent() doesn't create an undo level, so a transact() that follows has nothing to undo back to? Is calling undoManager.add() right before transact() the recommended way to make a programmatic DOM change undoable to the exact previous state? Or is there a better pattern, for example ed.undoManager.clear() plus add() right after setContent() , or using editor.dom helpers / editor.execCommand(...) / editor.insertContent instead of moving nodes directly? Are there downsides to moving existing nodes with insertBefore inside transact() (as opposed to replacing the content), for example when undo/redo rebuilds the DOM and any references I hold to the nodes become stale? I've read the docs for UndoManager.transact() and UndoManager.add() , but they don't say what happens to the "before" state when the content was set by setContent() .
